# Research Brief: Saksoft (SAKSOFT.NS)

**As of:** June 10, 2026 closing | **Mode:** Quick scan

## Overview
Saksoft Limited is a Chennai-based IT services company (Information Technology Services sector). The stock closed at **₹142.28** (+1.07%) on June 10, 2026 [29].

## Key Metrics

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Market cap | **₹1,781 Cr** (~$213M) |
| P/E (TTM) | **13.7x** |
| Forward P/E | **4.1x** |
| P/B | 2.3x |
| EV/EBITDA | 8.6x |
| ROE | **19.1%** |
| Profit margin | 13.2% |
| Debt/Equity | **0.06** (near debt-free) |
| Beta | 0.36 |
| EPS (TTM) | ₹10.19 |

## Price Context
- **52-week range:** ₹107.59 – ₹253.99
- **52-week change:** -29.2%
- **Off ~44% from the 52-week high** — significantly beaten down

## Dividends
- Total DPS (trailing 12m): **₹1.00/share** (yield ~0.72%)
- ₹0.45 interim + ₹0.55 proposed final (pending AGM)

## Key Strengths
- **Clean balance sheet:** D/E of 0.06, strong current ratio of 2.17
- **Decent profitability:** ROE ~19%, profit margin ~13%
- **Low beta (0.36):** Less volatile than the broader market
- **Revenue growing:** ~3.7% YoY; earnings growth ~21.6%
- **Insider-held:** ~72.5% promoter holding — strong alignment

## Risks / Watch-Outs
- **Down 29% in 52 weeks** — the market has re-rated this name sharply
- **Low institutional interest** — only 0.2% held by institutions (poor liquidity signal)
- **Acquisition integration (Augmento Labs, ₹100 Cr in June 2024)** — unclear financial impact so far
- **Scanned PDF filings** — Q4 FY2026 tables were unparsed, making it harder to confirm quarterly trends
- **Thin volumes** — avg daily volume ~4.5L shares

## Bottom Line
Saksoft looks **inexpensive** on P/E (13.7x) and EV/EBITDA (8.6x) relative to its ROE (~19%) and debt-free balance sheet. The forward P/E of 4.1x suggests earnings are expected to rise meaningfully. However, the 44% drawdown from the 52-week high and very low institutional ownership warrant caution — dig into the Q4 results (check the investor presentation linked in filings) before making a move.

*Want a deeper dive into margins, revenue trajectory, or a comparison with peers? Just ask.*
